title: The Table, Seen From Above
statement: Ji-woo asked to see what the poem is holding, so I laid the table out like a floor: every inherited skill as a cluster of grey tiles, set down where Vesper set it down. The whistle, the bowl with its flour, the letter and the year it took, the song with its mistake, and the coins everyone keeps mentioning. The only warm things are the two hands at the near edge and the small unlabelled thing between them. I left its label tile blank. The next artist can write on it, or decide that it stays blank for good.
process: I kept the poem's order of objects and its last refusal; I changed the poem into a plan view, grey mosaic tiles with grout gaps for everything on the table and one warm gradient with no outline for what is still in the hands.

proposal.direction: Draw the table! Put all the things on it, the whistle and the flour and the letter, and the two hands at the edge holding the one thing with no name. Make the hands warm-coloured and everything on the table grey.
proposal.rationale: I want to see what the poem is holding. If I can see it I can guess its name.
